classifications.rationale: FocusTrace deterministically checks negative-tabindex frames when their same-origin embedded document is locally inspectable and fails when sequentially focusable descendants are observed. Cross-origin, opaque or unavailable nested documents are surfaced separately as an explicit REVIEW coverage boundary rather than treated as clean.

FocusTrace compares normalized accessible names of exposed frames and requests REVIEW when names repeat because identical names are valid only when the embedded contexts have equivalent purpose. The implementation intentionally uses accessible-name evidence rather than reproducing axe's title-attribute-only benchmark boundary.

FocusTrace checks exposed frames for a non-empty accessible name using its shared local name computation, including title, aria-label and aria-labelledby evidence plus presentational handling. Its AccName implementation remains deliberately bounded, so the relationship is partial rather than exact equivalence.
FocusTrace implements the same top-level HTML lang-presence expectation and references the corresponding ACT rule.
FocusTrace validates the committed IANA primary-language subtag subset and intentionally does not validate every later subtag/flat-tree case.
FocusTrace validates HTML lang values but does not currently compare simultaneous lang and xml:lang values for base-language agreement.
FocusTrace covers meaningful versus decorative img accessible names with its local AccName model, but does not claim every axe image-alt applicability and platform edge case.
FocusTrace's broader form-field name rule includes input button naming and other supported form-control types.
FocusTrace derives the accessible name for input[type=image] inside its form-control rule, while axe frames this as a dedicated non-text alternative expectation.
FocusTrace detects unnamed supported form controls and computes native/ARIA naming sources, but it does not claim every axe label applicability/exception.
FocusTrace implements a bounded inline-prose candidate detector, measuring link-to-surrounding-text contrast and persistent non-color cues while retaining REVIEW where context matters.
FocusTrace checks supported native/ARIA links with its local accessible-name model, but not every axe naming edge case.
FocusTrace validates native list element children plus significant direct text, nested-list validity and script-supporting/whitespace allowances as part of its broader structural HTML rule.
standards: HTML Living Standard list content models

classifications.rationale: FocusTrace validates native li parent context and separately verifies explicit ARIA list/listitem ownership without duplicating a native orphan as an ARIA required-parent finding.
standards: HTML Living Standard li permitted parents

classifications.rationale: FocusTrace detects marquee-like persistent movement for REVIEW and separately reports obsolete HTML; outcome and contextual exceptions differ from axe.
